checks.title: RDS instances have automated backups with retention greater than 0 days (recommended: at least 7)

verify.pass_when_text: BackupRetentionPeriod greater than 0 (Drata test 107 requires automated backups). A retention of 0 fails with the check's severity; a retention of 1 to 6 days is reported as an offender with severity_override low, because the recommended minimum of 7 days is a catalog criterion and not a Drata one. With 7 or more it passes. Aurora and DocumentDB instances have a default retention of 1: they pass the Drata test and appear here only as a recommendation.

steps: Choose the retention (7 days is the recommended minimum) for database {resource_id}.
Apply it with the first block (standalone instance) or with the second (member of an Aurora cluster or Multi-AZ DB cluster, where retention belongs to the cluster).
Verify with describe-db-instances that BackupRetentionPeriod is the chosen value.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DB_ID="{resource_id}"
# instance that does not belong to a cluster
aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier "$DB_ID" --backup-retention-period 7 --apply-immediately --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DB_ID="{resource_id}"
# cluster member: retention is changed on the cluster
CLUSTER_ID=$(aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier "$DB_ID" --region "$REGION" --query 'DBInstances[0].DBClusterIdentifier' --output text)
[ -n "$CLUSTER_ID" ] && [ "$CLUSTER_ID" != "None" ] && aws rds modify-db-cluster --db-cluster-identifier "$CLUSTER_ID" --backup-retention-period 7 --apply-immediately --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Going from 0 to a higher value interrupts the database for a few minutes on a Single-AZ instance (RDS takes a snapshot and suspends I/O); raising it from a value above 0 to 7 does not. Apply it in an agreed window. Backups cost storage on top of the database size. --apply-immediately also applies any other pending change on the instance. A read replica without backups also fails this test. 7 days is a catalog design criterion, not a Drata threshold (Drata only requires greater than 0): that is why 1 to 6 is reported with severity_override low.

checks.title: Production RDS instances (or those without an Environment tag) are Multi-AZ

verify.pass_when_text: MultiAZ=true on the instance. It applies to production instances (Environment tag with value prod or production, case-insensitive) and to those without the Environment tag; instances from other environments (staging, dev...) do not apply. Cluster members (Aurora, Multi-AZ DB cluster) are judged by the cluster's high availability and are not evaluated here. Drata test 30.

steps: Confirm that database {resource_id} is a production one (or tag it with Environment if it is not) and choose a maintenance window.
Convert the instance to Multi-AZ (command): RDS creates a standby in another zone from a snapshot and synchronizes it.
Wait for the status to return to available and verify MultiAZ=true.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DB_ID="{resource_id}"
aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier "$DB_ID" --multi-az --apply-immediately --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Cost: the instance is charged double (a standby of the same class and storage). The conversion takes from several minutes to hours depending on size and has a performance (I/O) impact while the standby synchronizes; do it outside peak hours, or without --apply-immediately so that it is applied in the maintenance window. The database stays available during the conversion, and for engines that require it there may be a brief reboot. --apply-immediately also applies any other pending change. A database from another environment is not evaluated: tagging Environment correctly avoids false positives. For an Aurora cluster, high availability is achieved by adding a replica in another zone (create-db-instance in the cluster).

checks.title: RDS instances have auto minor version upgrade enabled

verify.pass_when_text: AutoMinorVersionUpgrade=true on every instance. A value of false or a missing value fails (Drata test 219 and Vanta test 22).

drata.name: AWS RDS Auto Minor Version Upgrade

vanta.test: Auto minor version upgrade is enabled for RDS instances

steps: Enable auto minor version upgrade on database {resource_id}; upgrades will be applied from now on in its maintenance window.
Verify with describe-db-instances that AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is true.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DB_ID="{resource_id}"
aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier "$DB_ID" --auto-minor-version-upgrade --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: The change is immediate and has no downtime, but from then on RDS applies minor versions in the maintenance window (PreferredMaintenanceWindow) and that upgrade can restart the database (in Multi-AZ, a failover). Review the window. If an application depends on a specific minor version, test in staging first. --apply-immediately is not used so as not to apply other pending changes.

verify.pass_when_text: DeletionProtection=true on every instance. A value of false or a missing value fails. In Aurora the protection belongs to the cluster.

steps: Enable deletion protection on database {resource_id}: the command applies it to the instance or, if it is a cluster member, to the cluster.
Verify with describe-db-instances that DeletionProtection is true.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DB_ID="{resource_id}"
# cluster member: the protection belongs to the cluster; if it does not belong to any, it belongs to the instance
CLUSTER_ID=$(aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier "$DB_ID" --region "$REGION" --query 'DBInstances[0].DBClusterIdentifier' --output text) || CLUSTER_ID="READ_FAILED"
if [ "$CLUSTER_ID" = "READ_FAILED" ]; then echo "STOPPED: could not read instance $DB_ID (rds:DescribeDBInstances); nothing was changed"; elif [ -n "$CLUSTER_ID" ] && [ "$CLUSTER_ID" != "None" ]; then aws rds modify-db-cluster --db-cluster-identifier "$CLUSTER_ID" --deletion-protection --region "$REGION"; else aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier "$DB_ID" --deletion-protection --region "$REGION"; fi
remediation.notes: No downtime and reversible with --no-deletion-protection. While it is active, delete-db-instance fails: to delete the database on purpose (or with terraform destroy) it must be disabled first. It is applied immediately, which is why it does not use --apply-immediately.

checks.title: DynamoDB tables have point-in-time recovery (PITR) enabled

verify.pass_when_text: PointInTimeRecoveryStatus=ENABLED on every table (Drata test 301). A table deleted between listing and reading does not apply; a table that cannot be read ends up NOT_VERIFIED without hiding the others.

steps: Enable PITR on table {resource_id}.
Verify with describe-continuous-backups that PointInTimeRecoveryStatus is ENABLED.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --table-name "{resource_id}" --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime or performance impact, and reversible with PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=false (the history is lost). Cost: charged per GB of the table (continuous backup, 35 days of retention). Drata additionally needs the inline permission backup:ListRecoveryPointsByResource on the DrataAutopilotRole role to evaluate this test.

verify.pass_when_text: Status=Enabled on every bucket (Drata test 108). A bucket with versioning suspended or never enabled fails. A bucket deleted between listing and reading does not apply; a bucket that cannot be read ends up NOT_VERIFIED without hiding the others.

steps: Enable versioning on bucket {resource_id}.
Add a lifecycle rule that expires noncurrent versions to bound the cost.
Verify with get-bucket-versioning that Status is Enabled.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket "{resource_id}" --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Caution: put-bucket-versioning replaces the bucket's versioning configuration (for example MFA Delete). No downtime. Cost: previous versions and delete markers take up storage until a lifecycle rule (NoncurrentVersionExpiration) expires them; define it in the same change. Versioning cannot be disabled once enabled, only suspended. Some buckets (logs, temporary or cache) may not need it: if Drata flags them, exclude them with a justification.

checks.title: S3 buckets have Block Public Access enabled on all 4 settings

verify.pass_when_text: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets are true in the bucket's own configuration (Drata test 104, which does not evaluate the account-level Block Public Access). A bucket without a configuration (NoSuchPublicAccessBlockConfiguration) fails. A bucket deleted between listing and reading does not apply; a bucket that cannot be read ends up NOT_VERIFIED without hiding the others.

vanta.test: Buckets use Block Public Access settings

steps: Check whether bucket {resource_id} serves public content on purpose (static website or public ACL) and, if so, put it behind CloudFront with private access before blocking.
Enable the 4 Block Public Access settings on the bucket.
Verify with get-public-access-block that the 4 settings are true.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# read-only: whether the bucket is public according to its policy
aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status --bucket "{resource_id}" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: WARNING: put-public-access-block replaces the bucket's Block Public Access configuration; if the bucket serves public content on purpose, it stops being accessible. No downtime, but if the bucket serves public content on purpose (static website with anonymous access, public ACLs), it stops being accessible: move it to CloudFront with Origin Access Control first. get-bucket-policy-status answers NoSuchBucketPolicy if the bucket has no policy: that is not an error. Reversible with put-public-access-block set to false. The account-level Block Public Access (aws s3control put-public-access-block) is also recommended, but Drata does not evaluate it.

checks.title: AWS Backup jobs from the last 24 hours completed successfully

verify.pass_when_text: One verdict per AWS Backup vault: each resource with jobs created in the last 24 hours (a rolling window, not the calendar day) has at least one COMPLETED; jobs in progress do not count as a failure. A vault with recovery points and no job in that window also fails. An empty vault with no jobs does not apply. With no AWS Backup vault at all, the check is N/A. Drata test 132.

steps: Find out why the jobs of vault {resource_id} failed (first block, read-only; detail.resources lists the affected resources): StatusMessage usually points to a permissions problem in the role, the vault or the resource.
Fix the cause (AWS Backup role, vault policy, resource state) and start an on-demand backup of the affected resource again (second block).
Verify that the new job ends in COMPLETED and that the plan repeats it every day.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
VAULT_NAME="{resource_id}"
# read-only: vault jobs that did not finish successfully
aws backup list-backup-jobs --by-backup-vault-name "$VAULT_NAME" --region "$REGION" --query 'BackupJobs[?State!=`COMPLETED`].[BackupJobId,ResourceArn,State,StatusMessage,CreationDate]' --output table

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
VAULT_NAME="{resource_id}"
RESOURCE_ARN="__FILL_IN_RESOURCE_ARN__"
ROLE_ARN="__FILL_IN_BACKUP_ROLE_ARN__"
aws backup start-backup-job --backup-vault-name "$VAULT_NAME" --resource-arn "$RESOURCE_ARN" --iam-role-arn "$ROLE_ARN" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: If the finding says the vault had no job at all, check that the plans have a daily rule that uses this vault (DAT-010) and that the resources are assigned to the plan (backup selection). An on-demand backup consumes storage and can load the resource (RDS, EFS): do it outside peak hours. Drata needs backup:ListRecoveryPointsByResource and backup:ListBackupJobs inline on the DrataAutopilotRole role; without them the test returns AccessDenied. Drata test 134 additionally requires re-running a failed backup within 24 hours.

checks.title: AWS Backup vaults send backup failure alerts to an SNS topic

verify.pass_when_text: Each vault with recovery points has notifications configured with an SNS topic and the BACKUP_JOB_FAILED event. A vault without notifications fails; empty vaults (no recovery points) do not apply. With no AWS Backup vault at all (or only empty ones), the check is N/A. Drata test 133.

steps: Decide the destination of the alerts: an existing SNS topic or a new one with subscribers (email, chat or pager) from the team that handles failures.
If the topic is new, create it and subscribe an email (first block) and allow AWS Backup to publish (second block).
Configure the notifications of vault {resource_id} (third block) and confirm the subscription from the email.
Verify with get-backup-vault-notifications.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TOPIC_NAME="__FILL_IN_TOPIC_NAME__"
ALERT_EMAIL="__FILL_IN_ALERTS_EMAIL__"
TOPIC_ARN=$(aws sns create-topic --name "$TOPIC_NAME" --region "$REGION" --query 'TopicArn' --output text) && aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "$TOPIC_ARN" --protocol email --notification-endpoint "$ALERT_EMAIL" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TOPIC_ARN="__FILL_IN_TOPIC_ARN__"
# only for a NEW topic: set-topic-attributes replaces the whole policy; on an existing topic, add the statement to its current policy
aws sns set-topic-attributes --topic-arn "$TOPIC_ARN" --attribute-name Policy --attribute-value '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"AllowAwsBackupPublish","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"backup.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sns:Publish","Resource":"'"$TOPIC_ARN"'"}]}' --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
VAULT_NAME="{resource_id}"
TOPIC_ARN="__FILL_IN_TOPIC_ARN__"
aws backup put-backup-vault-notifications --backup-vault-name "$VAULT_NAME" --sns-topic-arn "$TOPIC_ARN" --backup-vault-events BACKUP_JOB_FAILED --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: put-backup-vault-notifications replaces the vault's notification configuration: if it already had other events (for example COPY_JOB_FAILED or BACKUP_JOB_EXPIRED), include them in --backup-vault-events. The topic needs a policy that allows sns:Publish to the backup.amazonaws.com service; set-topic-attributes overwrites the entire policy, which is why the second block is only for new topics. Recommended: scope the policy with the aws:SourceAccount condition. A topic encrypted with KMS additionally needs the key to allow AWS Backup. Drata may accept other alerting mechanisms (for example an EventBridge rule on failed jobs); if one already exists, confirm against test 133 before duplicating it.

checks.title: At least one AWS Backup plan has a daily rule with retention of at least 7 days

verify.pass_when_text: At account level: at least one AWS Backup plan, in any evaluated region, has a rule with a daily or more frequent ScheduleExpression (cron with day of month, month and day of week unrestricted) and retention (Lifecycle.DeleteAfterDays) of 7 days or more; no expiration is treated as indefinite retention. Weekly or archive plans do not fail as long as a compliant daily plan exists. If no plan complies (or there are none) it fails once, with the aws-backup resource. Expressions that are not modeled (rate(), partial weeks) do not count. The 7 days are a catalog design criterion.

steps: Decide the scope: which resources the plan protects (by tag or by ARN), the destination vault, the AWS Backup role and the retention (35 days is a common value).
If there is no plan, create it with a daily rule and assign the resources to it (first block).
If there are plans but none has a compliant daily rule (detail.plans), look at the rules of the chosen plan (second block) and add a daily rule with update-backup-plan (third block).
Verify with get-backup-plan that the daily rule exists with the chosen retention.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
PLAN_NAME="__FILL_IN_PLAN_NAME__"
VAULT_NAME="__FILL_IN_VAULT_NAME__"
ROLE_ARN="__FILL_IN_BACKUP_ROLE_ARN__"
RESOURCE_ARN="__FILL_IN_RESOURCE_ARN__"
PLAN_ID=$(aws backup create-backup-plan --backup-plan "{\"BackupPlanName\":\"$PLAN_NAME\",\"Rules\":[{\"RuleName\":\"diario\",\"TargetBackupVaultName\":\"$VAULT_NAME\",\"ScheduleExpression\":\"cron(0 5 ? * * *)\",\"Lifecycle\":{\"DeleteAfterDays\":35}}]}" --region "$REGION" --query 'BackupPlanId' --output text) && aws backup create-backup-selection --backup-plan-id "$PLAN_ID" --backup-selection "{\"SelectionName\":\"$PLAN_NAME-recursos\",\"IamRoleArn\":\"$ROLE_ARN\",\"Resources\":[\"$RESOURCE_ARN\"]}" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
PLAN_NAME="__FILL_IN_PLAN_NAME__"
# read-only: current rules of the plan
PLAN_ID=$(aws backup list-backup-plans --region "$REGION" --query "BackupPlansList[?BackupPlanName=='$PLAN_NAME'].BackupPlanId | [0]" --output text) && aws backup get-backup-plan --backup-plan-id "$PLAN_ID" --region "$REGION" --query 'BackupPlan.Rules'

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
PLAN_ID="__FILL_IN_PLAN_ID__"
# update-backup-plan REPLACES the whole plan: the JSON must contain the current rules plus the new daily rule
PLAN_JSON='__FILL_IN_PLAN_JSON__'
aws backup update-backup-plan --backup-plan-id "$PLAN_ID" --backup-plan "$PLAN_JSON" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: update-backup-plan replaces the entire plan (each call creates a new version): if the JSON omits an existing rule, that rule is lost; always start from the output of the second block. A plan without a backup selection protects nothing: the first block also creates the resource assignment, which can be done by tag. Cost: recovery points take up storage for the whole retention. The AWS Backup role needs the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy. 7 days is a catalog design criterion, not a Drata or Vanta one.

verify.pass_when_text: MultiAZ=enabled on every Redis replication group (Drata test 30). A value of disabled or a missing value fails. Memcached and clusters without a replication group are not evaluated.

steps: If replication group {resource_id} has no replicas, add at least one (first block), which ends up in another Availability Zone, and wait for it to be available.
Enable automatic failover and Multi-AZ on the group: the first block already chains it; if the group already had replicas, use only the second block.
Verify that MultiAZ and AutomaticFailover are listed as enabled.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RG_ID="{resource_id}"
aws elasticache increase-replica-count --replication-group-id "$RG_ID" --new-replica-count 1 --apply-immediately --region "$REGION" && aws elasticache wait replication-group-available --replication-group-id "$RG_ID" --region "$REGION" && aws elasticache modify-replication-group --replication-group-id "$RG_ID" --automatic-failover-enabled --multi-az-enabled --apply-immediately --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RG_ID="{resource_id}"
# only for a group that already has at least one replica: it does not add nodes
aws elasticache modify-replication-group --replication-group-id "$RG_ID" --automatic-failover-enabled --multi-az-enabled --apply-immediately --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Cost: each replica is one more node of the same class as the primary. If the group already has replicas, increase-replica-count fails because --new-replica-count must exceed the current count: use only the second block (modify-replication-group). The new replica synchronizes by copying the dataset (performance impact on the primary, larger on big caches). Do it outside peak hours. Clusters with cluster mode enabled add the replica in each shard. Multi-AZ applies to Redis/Valkey; Memcached has no replication group.
